carry: A GATE THAT LISTS A NAME AS IF IT WERE A VALUE FAILS ON CODE THAT STATES NOTHING. The interface-motion gate caught animate-in/animate-out alongside duration-* and ease-*. An animation NAME states no duration and no curve — the timing it runs at is the duration-* beside it — so the gate failed 22 sites that had nothing to state, while transition-opacity, default-by-omission in exactly the same way, passed. It shipped red and stayed red for a batch that never opened those files. GENERALISES: before a gate lists a token, ask whether the token IS the value or merely names the thing that has one; and a gate whose failures a batch cannot act on is a gate scoped wrong, not a backlog.

A SET WITH NO HOME CANNOT BE OFFERED AS A LIST, AND THAT IS A DESIGN CONSEQUENCE, NOT A TIDINESS ONE. Nine cockpits each knew its own title and were each told their own number by the stage, so every fact about a panel had a home and the SET of panels had none — which is precisely why the surface could hide one panel and could not answer "what tools are there". The owner asked for a product view; the missing piece was not a hide button but a declared roster. Building the roster first made the product view a VALUE of the visibility map (every entry false) rather than a mode, so it is reversible by the same gesture that entered it and back-to-factory is one write. GENERALISES: when a request is "show me all of X and let me pick", check first whether X exists as data anywhere; if it does not, that absence is the whole task.

A FORMAT CAN REFUSE AN EXACT ANSWER, AND THE REFUSAL IS THE FEATURE. Splitting a keyframe ease exactly is de Casteljau, but a subdivided half of a monotone curve can carry a control-point x outside [0,1] — and resolveEase clamps x on every read, so that half is unstorable. Measured: 1 of 23 vocabulary curves (easeInOutExpo), 52/99 positions, clamping would have shipped a silent 3.5e-2 reshape. The ruling is to REFUSE the gesture there rather than take it and bend, because a tool that bends the curve at the moment a point is added makes the author spend the next gesture correcting the tool. Before approximating inside a stored domain, check whether the domain can hold the exact answer at all.

WEBGPU IS A CLOSED FORK UNTIL A NUMBER REOPENS IT. three 0.182 ships three.webgpu.js, so adopting it is a choice, not a limitation — and it is ruled out because the gate it would be spent on has not been read: §7.2, the first Intel UHD 620 1080p frame reading, is still unchecked. A renderer adopted to buy headroom before the deficit is measured is headroom used as a design input. Reopen ONLY when §7.2 reads under 60fps with the wheel summoned during an authored move AND a profile attributes the deficit to draw-call or shader cost rather than DOM layout — the HUD is DOM by design.md D3, and a DOM-bound deficit is one a renderer swap does not touch. Real cost today: @react-three/postprocessing and @theatre/r3f both bind WebGLRenderer, so the swap forks the effect chain and the keyframe bridge, and the keyframe bridge is the parity oracle the export path is pinned to. See design.md D7.

A COMPLETE COORDINATE SYSTEM MAKES A FEATURE REQUEST A VIEW REQUEST. "Custom paths" read as a sixth missing capability until azimuth/elevation/reach about targetX/Y/Z was checked for completeness: it is spherical coordinates about a movable origin, so every route through space is ALREADY expressible in the tracks the document has. What was missing was keyframe placement plus a picture. Building the spline would have shipped two encodings of one path. Before scaffolding storage for a shape, check whether the existing shape already spans it.

A PANEL READ AS A STRANGER FINDS DEFECTS A PANEL READ AS ITS AUTHOR CANNOT. §6c came from re-reading the motion inspector against the design law with no memory of building it, and every one of the five findings was a violation of a rule already written down rather than a preference: an accessible name that differed from the visible label, an `aria-label` on a non-interactive span (which has no accessible name to attach to and announces to nobody), a transparent-at-rest overlay gated on `:hover` and `:focus-within` — neither of which a coarse pointer can produce, so the shelf could be filled and not edited on touch — one verb naming both a playhead move and a discard of authored work, and a drag pad with no keyboard route to the bounds every named curve starts and ends at. GENERALISES: hover-revealed commands need `@media (hover: hover)` gating or they do not exist on touch; a state marker needs a name in the accessible tree, not only a colour; and two controls that share a verb are two controls the user separates by trying one.

A TRACKED BACKUP FILE CARRIES A PLAINTEXT KEY, and it is a second copy of a config as well. `opencode.json.bak:9` holds `"apiKey": "founder-mode-unlocked"` against the self-hosted tailnet endpoint; `opencode.json` already replaced it with `apiKeyEnv: OPENCODE_API_KEY`, so the .bak states nothing the live file does not — Update In Place says one of the two goes. It entered in b623adb and is already in pushed history, so deleting it stops the file being live but does not unleak the string; rotating the endpoint's key is the owner's call. Not fixed here: outside the requested update.

THE OWNER'S THREE-MODE ASK MAPPED ONTO THE ARC RATHER THAN DISPLACING IT, and five proposals now carry it: add-interface-motion-system, add-artifact-budget-gates, add-binocular-dimension-machines, add-surface-node-tree, add-customize-walkthrough. All five PASS `openspec validate --strict`. The gallery needed no new change — add-community-state-gallery already specs the local-library half. TWO AXES, NOT ONE: mode (Settings / Gallery / Customize) is what surrounds the object, dimension (2D / 2.5D / 3D) is how it is drawn, and they are independent — nine valid states from one tree with a swapped subtree, instead of nine hard-coded surfaces. THE ORDER IS FORCED, not preferred: the budget gates precede the 2.5D barrel because a third renderer added while nothing measures wire bytes or frames on the T480s means the machine that discovers the miss is a visitor's.

A DIMENSION AXIS CONTRADICTS A RATIFIED REQUIREMENT, and it was one command from being built anyway. `surface-mode-switching` ratifies BOTH `/3d` is the only 3D surface AND that switching is route navigation carrying customization across. add-binocular-dimension-machines therefore ships MODIFIED deltas for both, with the was-clauses stated: two affordances cannot express a three-position axis, and carrying customization across a boundary is what let two state models diverge in the first place. THE RESOLUTION THAT KEPT THE BLAST RADIUS SMALL: a route now NAMES A BARREL rather than owning a surface, so every published link, `browser-navigation` and the PWA are untouched, and the archived inline `viewMode:"3d"` path stays archived behind its flag — a dimension axis is not its resurrection. CLAUDE.md 'Before proposing' now carries the general rule.

THE SURFACE IS RUNTIME DATA, AND ITS NODE PATHS ARE THE DECISION LOG ADDRESSES. Ruled 2026-07-30: the three-mode shell — Settings, Gallery, Customize, configurator always centre — is a tree of node descriptors read at runtime, not JSX. A node reads its slice of the document and emits commands, never reaching a parent or a sibling, so swapping, reordering or A/B-ing one is a data edit rather than a refactor. THE UNIFICATION: add-customizer-decision-log needs a stable name for what changed, and a node path (customize/step:case/field:finish) IS that name — the AST and the history are one structure read two ways, which collapses two designs into one. lib/ipod-state/panel-layout.ts plus the duplicate panel registry Act 2 was going to retire are the half-version this REPLACES, not joins. COROLLARY, and it is why Haxe was declined: the tree has to be runtime data for the experimentation property to hold, and a macro system bakes it at compile time; a second type system over a TS-native toolchain (tsc, oxlint, vitest, openspec gates) is also a second home for one fact. If a hot core ever needs WASM the honest candidates are Rust or Zig behind a stable interface, and that is endgame, not next.

THE TARGET MACHINE IS NAMED AND ITS TWO GATES DO NOT EXIST YET. ThinkPad T480s, Intel UHD 620, 1080p — CLAUDE.md 'The machine we fit' now carries it. Measured 2026-07-30: 4.5 MB of .next/static on disk, and NOTHING measures the wire cost of a single route or the frame rate on integrated graphics. The absence is the finding, not the number. Both gates belong in pnpm validate beside the colour envelope, printing their reading on pass, because a budget measured only after it is missed has never been met. The CD-era ethos is already the architecture — geometry parametric from IPOD_CLASSIC_MM, colour derived from the manifest, motion as documents rather than baked frames — so the threat to the budget is three.js, not the design.

Owner called it 'a specific art style'; the reference is still unnamed.

A ROW STATES A VALUE, SO THE VALUE HAS TO BE STORED — and the reducer already knew it. §6.7 asked for a shelf row reading `Orbit — slow · 3× · seamless`, which is not readable off a MotionDoc: repeat, clip length and time map live in MotionState, so the row as specified would have shown a value the entry did not hold. SavedMotion.cadence closes it, and the UNUSED APPLY_MOTION action — payload MotionState, comment 'the shelf's one-tap recall' — is the evidence the shape was decided in §4 and half-built in §4b.1. GENERALISES: when a task specifies a readout, the readout is a spec for the STORED shape, not for the formatting; and an action that was added with no caller is a design already ruled on, so read it before re-ruling.

SAVE OVER MUST CLEAR THE OVERRIDE IT JUST ABSORBED — fourth appearance. Writing the flown document into the open shelf entry makes the surviving override a stored copy of its own base, which samples identically today and stops tracking the entry forever after. Same defect as the saved theme's rig, the sanitizeSpot castShadow:undefined deviation and applyTrackEdit chaining. THE RULE, now four times paid for: whenever a BASE is rewritten to include a DIFF, the diff has to be dropped in the same gesture.

A CONTROL THAT STORES A DERIVED VALUE MUST DERIVE IT FROM THE BASE, AND MUST CLEAR RATHER THAN STORE AN IDENTITY. The inspector's sliders hold three scalars (gain, phase, curve) and the model stores a whole MotionTrack, so the projection runs both ways: applyTrackEdit ALWAYS starts at the shipped track, never at the previous result. Chaining would leave 17 x 0.4 x 2.5 = 16.999999999999996 after a drag away and back — permanently and invisibly off the catalogue, with no gesture that returns it. And an edit that lands back on the shipped values DROPS its override (CLEAR_MOTION_TRACK, withoutTrack collapsing {tracks:{}} to undefined) rather than storing a copy of the base: the copy samples identically today and stops tracking the catalogue document forever after. THIRD APPEARANCE of the preset-tracking defect — the saved theme's rig, the sanitizeSpot castShadow:undefined false deviation, now this. The comparison goes through canonicalTrack, extracted out of motionDocHash rather than written a second time.

THE CATALOGUE'S ALTERNATION IS WHY A PRISTINE TRACK HAS NO CURVE TO NAME. The shipped quarter-keyframe tracks alternate easeOutSine / easeInSine, and that alternation IS what makes them exact sines (§2). So the inspector's curve row reads `Mixed`, draws the first segment dashed, and unifies every segment on the first drag — a real change of character, which is exactly the spec's `linear toward easeInOutSine` axis rather than a rounding. The §2 port floor is unaffected because no edit mutates CATALOGUE_DOCS. GENERALISES: when a shipped value is a STRUCTURE and the control is a SCALAR, the honest readout is that they differ, not the scalar nearest to the structure.

THE MIGRATION WAS INERT AND ONLY A VALUE ASSERTION FOUND IT. `repeatFromSpeed` needs the document's natural cycle length; `SanitizeMotionOptions.naturalCycleSeconds` carried it; NOT ONE of the four boundaries (normalizeModel, loadStudioState, decodePortableState, snapshotToModel) passed it. Every legacy `speed` therefore converted to `repeat: 1` regardless of what it had been flying, while §3.2 claimed the conversion 'cannot be missed once'. Fixed inside sanitizeMotionState, the only place that knows the docId: the option defaults to CATALOGUE_DOCS[docId].naturalCycleSeconds, total for the legacy case because `speed` predates the shelf. GENERALISES: an option with a fallback is not a migration until a test asserts the converted VALUE — a test that only asserts 'does not throw' would have passed on the broken code.

THE §3.4 TURNAROUND READINGS ARE ENGINE-SPECIFIC, and the ledger did not say so. They reproduce EXACTLY on the procedural generators (turntable azimuth 3.1191, sweep elevation 1.3675, crane elevation 1.3356, crane reach 5.8340e-2) and SHIFT on the ported documents (3.1191 unmoved — its port is exact; 1.3627; 1.3225; 5.8687e-2), because the port residual displaces where the maximum sits. lib/motion/transport.test.ts measures the procedural clip and says so at the assertion. §2.9 moves these numbers by exactly that much when it swaps the engine.

MEASURED, and it killed the ledger's premise: §3.4 asked for 'a bezier that matches today's smootherstep, so the default is a no-op'. The shipped turnaround is a QUINTIC (x^3(6x^2-15x+10)) and a cubic bezier cannot be one — a degree mismatch, not a fitting failure. Best zero-end-slope bezier 8.1312e-3 phase error (a=0.49840); shipped pick [0.5,0,0.5,1] 8.6642e-3, +5.3e-4 for a readable tuple. The best UNCONSTRAINED bezier is 3.7x better (2.3380e-3) and was REJECTED ON MECHANISM: its end slopes are -0.119, so the camera backs up through the loop seam. Y overshoot is expression on a value track and a defect on a time map — that asymmetry is now load-bearing twice. A tangent-matched track clears the floor at 6 segments but a 7-keyframe time warp is not a curve anyone can drag. Ruled: the default moves the camera under boomerang and gates on the owner.

repeat:0 RETURNS THE HERO IN CLOSED FORM, and pinning phase 0 would have been wrong. D6 called hold 'amplitude zero' and that is exact: a document's tracks are offsets, so scaling by zero IS the hero. Sampling phase 0 is NOT — orbit's dolly is a raised cosine, so orbitPose(0) sits 0.15 units inside its hero and 2 deg below it. The closed form keeps a held clip byte-identical to what shipped.

THE MIGRATION DOES NOT LIVE IN healSlice, and the ledger was wrong to put it there. healSlice copies keys; it cannot turn `speed` into `repeat`. And `speed` appears in FOUR places — a stored studio slice, a share payload, an export record, a re-open. One sanitizer (sanitizeMotionState) used by normalizeModel, loadStudioState, decodePortableState and snapshotToModel is the only shape where the conversion cannot happen twice or be missed once. It also absorbs the v1 loop:'hold' -> repeat:0 case the ledger never named.

NEARLY SHIPPED AS A BUG: sanitizeMotionState is folded through normalizeModel, which runs on most reducer actions. If it also reset the playhead, editing the song title mid-playback would rewind the preview. The reset belongs to the BOUNDARY (withoutTransport at encode / storage load / decode / re-open), which is exactly how isNowPlayingEditable has always been written. Healing and excluding are different jobs.

THE EXPORT IDENTITY IS A HASH, NOT A NAME. `move: "orbit"` named both a pristine and a hand-tuned Orbit, so two visibly different exports carried one identity and the timeline proof would have served stale frames for edited motion. MotionIdentity.docHash is motionDocHash of the RESOLVED document. `overrides` rides along for re-open but is deliberately NOT hashed — docHash already covers it, and hashing both makes two encodings of one motion into two identities. FINGERPRINT_VERSION is now 2.

CLOSED at 25.9822 deg, and the closing move was to pass the DOCUMENT rather than the CLIP. One place decides which engine flies a motion (motionClipFor); §5.5 wired the proof and §5.8 wired the rig and the MP4, all three from one flownClip in ipod-3d-stage.tsx resolved above every consumer. The boundaries take doc?: MotionDoc, and flownMotionDoc(clip) is the single home of 'a document is present IFF the document engine flies it' — undefined for an untouched preset, which is the only reason §2.9's 0.2116 deg swap is still gated. Handing resolveFlownDoc to the rig instead would have performed that gated swap silently, because EVERY preset resolves to a document whether or not anything was tuned. GENERALISES: when a boundary takes the payload instead of the decision, the invariant tying payload-presence to the decision needs a named, tested home, or every caller re-derives it and one of them gets it wrong.

A NAME IS NOT AN IDENTITY FOR A CACHE KEY, and this is the second time that exact shape bit. The rig re-baked its pose sampler when `move` changed — correct while a move was only ever a preset id, wrong the moment a curve could be dragged, because tuning keeps docId and changes the document. A drag mid-preview would have held a stale sampler and shown a motion nobody authored. Fixed by making the document's REFERENCE part of the key, which is affordable only because flownClip is memoized on (docId, overrides, savedMotions) — so CameraPreviewState.doc now carries a referential-stability contract in its doc-comment, and violating it costs a sampler rebuild per frame rather than a wrong pose. Pairs with the §5.5 lesson: the key a cache or a debounce compares on is part of its contract, not an implementation detail.

STABILITY IS TRACKED ON THE PLAN KEY, NOT THE ANCHOR KEY, and the ledger's plan did not say which. timelineFingerprint folds in the proof inputs, so plan stability implies input stability — but NOT the reverse: switching documents moves the plan key and leaves proofFingerprint untouched, which is the whole reason browsing the catalogue does not re-render the anchor. Gating the timeline walk on anchor stability would therefore have warmed a whole set on the FIRST tick of every document, so a catalogue browse or a curve drag bursts one render per position with no idle debounce — the exact drag-storm the scheduler exists to absorb, reintroduced by reusing the wrong key. GENERALISES: when a debounce is reused for a second stream, the key it debounces on is part of the contract, not an implementation detail.

A PROOF FRAME'S PROVENANCE IS ITS OWN POSE. One warm(key, snapshot, priority) body serves the anchor and every timeline frame, and a frame is the anchor snapshot with frame.pose substituted — so captureHighRes needed no new parameter (it already reads snapshot.pose) and the stored ProofEntry restores the camera it actually proves. Storing the anchor snapshot against a mid-clip frame would have made re-open set the hero pose for a frame the hero never produced.

MEASURED, and it overturned a design decision: design.md D3 prescribed quarter keyframes plus easeInOutSine for the whole catalogue port. That curve has a FLAT TANGENT at both ends — right for motion resting at each keyframe, wrong for a smooth curve sampled mid-slope. A quarter of a sine is not approximated by a named curve, it IS one exactly (easeOutSine = sin(pi x/2) rising, easeInSine = 1-cos(pi x/2) falling), so sine tracks alternate those and cosine tracks use the same pair reversed. Crane's second harmonic still missed at 1.243 deg vs the 0.25 floor; fixed by tangent-matched beziers (lib/motion/fit.ts, cubic Hermite as an easing) which cut it 15.7x to 0.0792 deg while HALVING the keyframe count to 9 — the editability that made the port worth doing. All 5 moves now PASS all 3 axes. Readings recorded in that change's tasks.md §2; never re-derive them.

THE CATALOGUE RESIDUAL IS ONE CONSTANT: 7.5561e-3 x amplitude, identical for sine and cosine tracks (a cosine track is a phase-shifted sine over the same quarter shapes). All 15 readings are that number scaled. Headroom: angle tracks conform up to 33.09 deg amplitude (largest shipped 28, sweep elevation, 85% of budget), reach tracks up to 1.323 units (largest shipped 1.1, crane reach). Raising an amplitude past those breaks the port and fails lib/motion/catalogue.test.ts loudly.

AMENDED, was a hole in the ledger: add-motion-authoring-system asserted 'save it as yours' three times in prose (proposal.md:83, design.md:123, design.md:209) and had zero tasks building it — motion could be authored but never owned. Now §4b, mirroring lib/studio-themes.ts rather than inventing a second registry shape. Deliberately NO default-motion pointer: §4.1 already persists the selected doc, so the boot needs no second one, and add-workspace-storage-registry is open on 21 keys across 3 conventions already. A shelf entry stores the document WHOLE — the one place D7's identity-plus-overrides ruling does not apply, because a shelf entry is a definition rather than a reference to one.

WATCH the import direction in lib/motion/doc.ts: it reads stableStringify + hashString out of lib/export/export-fingerprint.ts (one-way today, per task 1.5's 'do not add a second hash implementation'). §5.2 makes export-fingerprint carry a motion identity. If that ever needs to import back from lib/motion, extract the two helpers to a neutral module — do not resolve the cycle in place.

HALF LANDED, and the half that landed is the cheap one. The owner's 2026-07-29 ask was that each preset be 'clearly showcased of what you can do'. §6b answers the RECOGNITION half — every selectable motion draws its own sampled trace, so a move is picked by shape rather than by remembering which name went with it — and it answers it for free, because the trace is a pure function of the document rather than a render. WHAT IS STILL NOT SPEC'D is the COMPARISON half: two documents side by side on one playhead, which needs a surface rather than a row and is a separate change. RULED WHILE BUILDING: a rendered thumbnail per move was the obvious showcase and is the wrong one — five 3D captures of the real device is a withdrawal from a byte budget that does not have gates yet (add-artifact-budget-gates) and a frame cost on the T480s, spent on a shape createMotionSampler already knows exactly. A generated picture also cannot drift from the motion; a captured one can. The audience-facing motion reel stays Act 5 material.

RESOLVED, was a spec violation: a saved theme discarded a hand-tuned rig. `StudioTheme.rig` is now `{ name, overrides }` — the preset name plus a top-level sparse diff — so the preset stays the single definition of itself AND the tuning is the theme's own data. `overrides: {}` is the untouched case and still tracks future revisions of the preset. v1 records carrying a bare `rigName` migrate on read, no write required. The subtle one: `sanitizeSpot` writes `castShadow: undefined`, so a stored config carries keys a preset literal does not — a naive equality reads that as a deviation and would pin every reloaded theme's rig, ending preset tracking after the first reload. Measured and pinned in that change's tasks.md.

The /3d boot no longer matches Noir by coincidence. `createBootedWorkbenchModel` resolves a single stored default-theme pointer and applies its actions over the factory model, so the booted look and the theme the shelf marks default cannot disagree. Deleting the default deliberately leaves the pointer dangling — `resolveDefaultTheme` is the one place that heals it, to Noir. NOTE: this wires `/3d` only; `/` still boots through the app-wide `ipodCentralMachine`, which is the two-folds-of-one-model item already on this list.

The board is now self-enforcing: `pnpm validate` runs board:check, husky pre-commit runs validate. Drift classes gated — completed-but-unarchived (prints the archive command), dangling next/arc refs, change dir missing proposal/tasks, and staleness (openspec/changes edited without tasks/state.json, or a state date behind the last openspec commit). Update tasks/state.json in the same commit as the work; nothing else is hand-maintained.

RESOLVED: the CIEDE2000 hue-average branch. Now conformant to Sharma eq. 14 (all four cases, incl. the h1+h2>=360 branch the 34 reference pairs never reach). The pre-fix error was measured at <2e-4 dE over 400k random Lab pairs — real but four orders below any threshold, because the branches only differ where the RT rotation term is vanishing.

The WCAG-vs-IEC knee difference is provably unobservable for 8-bit input (no code falls between 0.03928 and 0.04045), so the collapse is a verified no-op, not a judgement call.

Colour and lighting are still separate registries. Nothing expresses 'this rig suits this finish'. add-finish-rig-pairing now carries this; the line stays until that change lands.

WIP LIMIT BREACHED — see `make board` for the count; a hand-written one is drift with a timestamp on it, and this line already carried a stale 7. The limit is 3 changes strictly between 0% and 100%. A MEMO DEP THE VALUE IS NOT DERIVED FROM IS A FAKE DEP. The timeline proof strip reads a cache whose contents no prop describes, so memoising the reads needed `version` — a counter — as a dep, which is a lie told to a linter. The honest shape is to read during render and state the constraint the memo would have hidden: this component must not be wrapped in React.memo. Generalises: when a reader depends on state outside its props, do not fabricate a dep — either make the state a prop or forbid the memo in writing, next to the code.
